clue.text: Taking a divot? Cover with earth in English 5

definitions.note: 5-down is TOWN, so this means an English town

parts.note: a golfer chipping can cut out a divot, a piece of turf or sod
to bury something is to cover it with soil

explanation.surface: Golfing advice: after hacking out a divot, replace it and tread the earth back over it.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 5 makes the definition an English town; CHIPPING SODBURY is a market town in Gloucestershire.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a small market town near Bristol, in southern England, fitting the themed cross-reference.

clue.text: Netherlands, you suspect, will capture north English 5

definitions.note: 5-down is TOWN, so this means an English town

indicators.note: the letters that capture something hold it inside them, like a prisoner
as an adjective, suspect means dubious or not genuine, so the letters are not to be trusted in their given order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A doubter guesses that the Dutch will seize the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: All fifteen letters, the extra N included, are rearranged. ASHTON-UNDER-LYNE is a town east of Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a market town in Greater Manchester, so it qualifies as an English town for the theme.

clue.text: Vegetable taken from the nose and head

parts.note: a runny nose runs, so what comes from it is jokingly a runner
bean is informal slang for the head

explanation.surface: Something unpleasant extracted from a person's nostrils and skull is passed off as food.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter treats what runs from the nose as a runner, a typically Paul-style toilet joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner bean is a climbing green bean commonly grown in British gardens and eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Philosopher almost accepts doctrine about northern relation

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the shortened name holds the rest inside
almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the name is dropped

parts.note: Immanuel Kant, the German philosopher

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the doctrine word goes round the direction letter

parts.note: an ism is any doctrine or creed
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A thinker nearly signs up to a creed concerning a relative from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: the doctrine wraps the direction letter, and that whole unit sits inside the shortened philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: A kinsman is a male blood relative, one belonging to the same family or kin.

clue.text: Go to it unsparingly, with nowt taken out

definitions.note: the clue is the phrase go to it unsparingly: to go to town is to do something lavishly

parts.note: part of the phrase whose missing word is the definition
tells us which phrase: going to it unsparingly is going all out

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, so the given word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: nowt is northern English for nothing; taken as written

explanation.surface: A northerner urged to spend lavishly, with nothing held back.
explanation.walkthrough: Go to town means to act lavishly, so the answer is the it in that phrase. The answer is the theme word that the long town clues cross-refer to.
explanation.definitionFit: In the idiom meaning to act without restraint, the missing word filling the slot is exactly this one.

clue.text: Actress riding great horse in English 5

definitions.note: 5-down is TOWN, so this means an English town

parts.note: Mae West, the Hollywood actress
someone riding is on a horse
super means great
a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: A film star rides a magnificent steed through an English town.
explanation.walkthrough: WESTON-SUPER-MARE is a seaside resort in Somerset.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a seaside resort on the Bristol Channel coast, a real English town for the theme.

clue.text: Upper-class in little county pulled up area for growing icebergs, perhaps, in English 5

definitions.note: 5-down is TOWN, so this means an English town

indicators.note: in a down clue, pulling something up makes it read from bottom to top
in places the class letter inside the county abbreviation

parts.note: Notts is the short form of Nottinghamshire
U is the old label for upper-class usage
iceberg lettuces grow in a field, and icebergs are cold

explanation.surface: A posh grower uproots plants in a small county where lettuces are farmed.
explanation.walkthrough: Icebergs are lettuces here, and a frozen field suits them. SUTTON COLDFIELD is a town near Birmingham.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a large town in the West Midlands, just north of Birmingham, so an English town.

clue.text: With article to address in India, it's said, securing university reference books

parts.note: the definite article

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the garment word wraps round the letter
it's said means we listen to how the word sounds when spoken

parts.note: address spoken sounds like a dress, and the dress of India is the sari
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A speaker in India is said to hold forth to a university about reference works.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken aloud, address is a dress, and in India that means the sari. SARI then takes U inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Thesauri, the plural of thesaurus, are books listing synonyms, used as reference works by writers.

clue.text: Unwind and speak freely

definitions.meaning: first meaning: unroll or unfold something
second meaning: talk candidly about one's feelings

explanation.surface: Advice to relax and talk openly, like a therapist's prompt.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to unfold or unroll something and to confide candidly in someone.

clue.text: It's just so boy collects the trophy

indicators.note: collecting something gathers it in, so the youngster holds the prize inside

parts.note: a son is a boy
a pot is slang for a trophy cup

explanation.surface: A proud parent notes it is only right that their lad picks up the cup.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot-on is informal for exactly right, and just so means precisely as it should be.

clue.text: Righteousness and good sense must be shown round court

indicators.note: shown round means placed around, so the good-sense word encircles the abbreviation

parts.note: sanity is sound judgement
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: Advice that virtue and level-headedness should be displayed before a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanctity is holiness or saintly virtue, close in meaning to moral uprightness and goodness.

clue.text: Pronounced miserly manner

indicators.note: pronounced means spoken aloud, so we go by the sound of the next word

parts.note: mean is a synonym for miserly

explanation.surface: Someone has a markedly stingy way about them.
explanation.walkthrough: Pronounced reads as marked in the surface, but it is the sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Mien is a literary word for a person's bearing or demeanour, how they carry themselves.

clue.text: Current around a lake needs more regular adjustment

definitions.note: a noun phrase, where the answer is a verbal noun

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the current word wraps the next two items

parts.note: a reigning champion is the current one
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: An electric current flowing round a lake requires tweaking more often.
explanation.walkthrough: Current suggests electricity, but here it means present, as in the current title holder.
explanation.definitionFit: Realigning means bringing things back into line, an adjustment that makes an arrangement straighter and tidier.

clue.text: Girl, one shut in the box in anger, causing anxiety

indicators.note: shut in means enclosed, so the earlier items are placed inside the anger word

parts.note: ire is anger
a girl's name

indicators.note: in places the preceding items inside what follows

parts.note: the box is slang for the television
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A girl locked in a box out of rage causes great distress.
explanation.walkthrough: The box is British slang for television.
explanation.definitionFit: Irritative means tending to irritate or annoy, so it describes something that causes anxiety or bother.

clue.text: One's a GI, prepared for violent struggles

indicators.note: prepared means made ready or worked up, so the letters are put into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An American soldier readies himself for brutal fights.
explanation.definitionFit: Agonies are throes of extreme suffering, and an agony originally meant a struggle or contest.

clue.text: Landslide admitted by party that's in the soup

indicators.note: something admitted by another is let inside it

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, a political party
a landslide victory is a rout

explanation.surface: A party concedes a crushing election defeat and finds itself in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: In the soup sounds like the idiom for being in trouble, but it is literal: the answer floats in soup.
explanation.definitionFit: A crouton is a small cube of fried or toasted bread served floating in soup.

clue.text: Rifle worked with the bullet

parts.note: a machine that ran was working
getting the bullet means being dismissed, given the sack

explanation.surface: A gun that operated, along with its ammunition.
explanation.walkthrough: Rifle looks like a gun and bullet like its ammunition; here rifle is a verb and the bullet is dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle a place is to search it hurriedly to steal from it, which is what ransacking means.

clue.text: At sea, often afraid? Not I! At sea, extremely!

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are jumbled
not I tells us to leave out the letter I from the words before

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nervous sailor protests that they are not frightened on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: At sea appears twice: first as the jumble signal, then in the definition, meaning on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Fore and aft means from bow to stern, at both extremes of a vessel, hence at sea extremely.

clue.text: Spin the head off the donkey

indicators.note: taking the head off removes the first letter of the animal word

parts.note: neddy is a British informal word for a donkey

explanation.surface: An instruction to whirl a beheaded donkey around.
explanation.walkthrough: Neddy is a childish British name for a donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: An eddy is a swirling current of water or air, a spin or whirl.

clue.text: Warped, so likes inserting head of blunt needles

indicators.note: inserting means putting one thing inside another
something warped is twisted out of shape, so the letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of blunt

explanation.surface: A sewing grumble: twisted needles are what someone prefers to a blunt one.
explanation.walkthrough: Cleopatra's Needle in London is an obelisk, so needles is a fair definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Obelisks are tall tapering stone pillars, often called needles, as with Cleopatra's Needle.

clue.text: It's no good taking part in an intimate embrace

indicators.note: taking part means only a portion of the words that follow is used

parts.note: the letters run across the words

explanation.surface: A disapproving remark that joining in a close cuddle is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Snog is British slang for a passionate kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: A snog is a long passionate kiss and cuddle, an intimate embrace in British slang.

clue.text: Bird has to mount it

parts.note: taken as written
Mt is the abbreviation for mount
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird must climb onto something, perhaps a perch.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomtit is a small bird, a British name for the blue tit or other small tits.

clue.text: Advertising shown until now!

parts.note: PR is public relations, promotion
a programme that is on is being shown
to can mean until, as in nine to five

explanation.surface: A slogan announcing a promotion screening only up to the present moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Pronto is an informal borrowing from Italian meaning immediately or right away, an exclamation like now.

clue.text: Comprehensive protection remaining in contact

indicators.note: in places the remaining word inside the contact word

parts.note: to call someone is to contact them
something left over is remaining

explanation.surface: An insurance pitch for full cover that stays in touch with the client.
explanation.definitionFit: A coverall is a full-body protective garment, so it shields the wearer entirely, all over.
